subject: Discrepancy in ingest sampling — request for snapshots and traces
thread_content:
From: accounts@nimbushealth.com <accounts@nimbushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle usage jump — please advise

Hi Irene,

Quick one: our August invoice looks ~47% higher than forecasted compared to June/July. The line item flagged is usage for the inference ingest pipeline (tokenized requests). We don't have any deploys or higher-traffic campaigns that would explain this. Can you provide the sampling snapshots for the 7/20–8/15 window and any telemetry traces that show sampling weight changes?

Account: Nimbus Health (acct id: NIM-2317)
Attached: the PDF bill we received (billing_export_august_2026.csv attached)

Thanks — can we get an initial reply with next steps today?

— Maya (Billing Ops)
accounts@nimbushealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya / accounts@nimbushealth.com <accounts@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage jump — please advise

Hi Maya,

Thanks for flagging this — sorry for the surprise. I’ve looped in Ben (AM) and Connor (billing ops) so we can pull the exact snapshots and telemetry. Next steps from our side:

- We’ll export the ingest sampling snapshots for 2026-07-20 through 2026-08-15 (including per-prefix sampling weights).
- Provide the tokenization and sampling trace archive for suspected windows.
- If we confirm an internal mis-tagging or sampling-regression, we’ll propose a provisional credit and timeline for final reconciliation.

Connor — can you start a targeted export and attach a preliminary CSV that shows hourly sampled vs. counted tokens for NIM-2317?

Irene Choi
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya / accounts@nimbushealth.com <accounts@nimbushealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage jump — please advise

Maya — quick context from our side:

- Initial look at the billing export shows a sharp spike starting 2026-07-28 08:00 UTC and lasting ~4 hours. The downstream token tally in the sampled pipeline doesn't map exactly to the ingest logs — there appears to be an overcount in the sampled projection for that window.
- Two likely causes: a sampling-weight configuration change (e.g., weight 1.0 instead of 0.1 for an internal prefix) or a duplicate ingestion stream that bubbled into the sampled counter.

Connor is preparing:
- billing_export_august_2026.csv (attached) — per-hour token counts we exported for NIM-2317
- request for telemetry_trace_20260728.zip (will include the sampler decisions and request IDs)

Provisional offer: if the root cause is on our side, Redwood will apply a provisional credit covering the disputed window (we typically start with a 30% provisional credit while we run a full reprocess). Final amount will be reconciled once reprocessing completes (usually 5–7 business days).

Can you confirm whether you have any internal job that ran on 2026-07-28 around 08:00–12:00 UTC that might have generated a large number of requests? That will help narrow down duplication vs sampling.

— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: billing_export_august_2026.csv (application/csv)

-----------------------------

From: Paul Sanders <paul.sanders@finops.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Maya / accounts@nimbushealth.com <accounts@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage jump — trace notes

Forwarding a short technical note I captured while reviewing the partial traces you sent. I’m attaching the snapshot I pulled from the ingest tier. TL;DR: there’s evidence the sampling function returned weight=1.0 for prefix "nh-telemetry-prod" during 2026-07-28 08:00–10:30 UTC; earlier windows show expected weight=0.1. That would multiply sampled tokens by 10x in the projection.

Suggested immediate steps (technical):
- Export the raw ingest request IDs for nh-telemetry-prod for 2026-07-28 07:45–11:00 UTC (for de-duplication).
- Cross-check request IDs against the KV-cache routing logs to see if the same requests were routed twice (dup stream).
- Re-run projection using corrected sampling weight and rebuild hourly tallies.

I’m attaching: ingest_window_snapshot_2026-07-28.json and a short grep-able trace bundle (telemetry_trace_20260728.zip). Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

— Paul Sanders
FinOps Consultant
paul.sanders@finops.io

Attachment: ingest_window_snapshot_2026-07-28.json (application/json)
Attachment: telemetry_trace_20260728.zip (application/zip)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya / accounts@nimbushealth.com <accounts@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Finance Team <finance@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage jump — request for snapshots and traces

Hi Maya — thanks for the details and thanks Paul for the trace. Quick update & proposed path forward:

1) Evidence collected: Connor’s target export + Paul’s snapshot both point to the same 2026-07-28 window with the sampler returning weight=1.0 for prefix "nh-telemetry-prod". We’ve retrieved the raw request-id list and started a de-duplication run.

2) Next steps and timeline:
- Today: run targeted reprocess of that 07:45–11:00 UTC window and produce corrected hourly tallies (expected 24–36 hours).
- +2 business days: produce corrected invoice reconciliation and an interim reconciliation report (CSV) for your review.
- +5 business days: final reconciliation and settlement with any applied credits.

3) Provisional credit: we will issue an interim 30% credit for the disputed window to be applied to your next invoice immediately. Final credit will be adjusted after reprocess completes.

4) Action items for Nimbus: please confirm whether any of your internal jobs ran within 2026-07-28 07:45–11:00 UTC (any large batch upload or test runs). If so, please share request-ids or job ids from your side — that will speed up dedup.

Attachments we will deliver: ingest_window_snapshot_2026-07-28.json, telemetry_trace_20260728.zip, and the preliminary billing_export_august_2026.csv (already shared).

If you’d like a quick call to walk through the traces, Ben and I can join this afternoon (2–4pm PT).

Appreciate the patience — we’ll keep this high priority.

Best,
Irene Choi
